possible_risks.description: A model might generate language that leads to physical harm.  The language might include overtly violent, covertly dangerous, or otherwise indirectly unsafe statements.
possible_risks.justification: The checkpoint is an 'abliterated' instruct model, a term used for models whose refusals have been removed, and the card reports no safety evaluation, so it plausibly generates language that could lead to physical harm.

possible_risks.description: Manipulative prompts that use social engineering techniques, such as role-playing or hypothetical scenarios, to persuade the model into generating harmful content.
possible_risks.justification: An abliterated open-weight instruct model with no reported safety testing is plausibly more susceptible to manipulative role-play or hypothetical-scenario prompts that elicit harmful content.

possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: The card is a text-generation instruct model conversion with no reported factuality or grounding evaluations, so it plausibly produces factually inaccurate or fabricated content.

specifications.model_size: 1.8 GiB of safetensors weights (1,976,163,203 bytes) in F32

training_context.adaptations: The model is an MLX conversion of Goekdeniz-Guelmez/Josiefied-Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-abliterated-v1, converted using mlx-lm version 0.18.2.
